meta.credit: Prepared by Suhaimi Zainal Shah with assistance from Claude AI (Anthropic).

incidents.title: Deepfake videos of PM Lee and DPM Wong promote crypto and investment scams
incidents.summary: Fake videos using the likeness of Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, and separately Deputy PM Lawrence Wong, were used to promote cryptocurrency and investment schemes. The date is PM Lee's public warning, the earliest public record found; the videos had been circulating for some days.

incidents.title: Second deepfake of Lee Hsien Loong promotes an investment product
incidents.summary: A new deepfake showed Lee Hsien Loong, by then Senior Minister, endorsing an investment product with guaranteed returns. He warned the public again.
incidents.notes: Exact day not confirmed from a primary source.

incidents.title: Deepfake videos and voice clones of PM Lawrence Wong promote scams
incidents.summary: AI-generated video and a cloned voice of Prime Minister Wong were used to promote cryptocurrency, money-making schemes and PR services.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Singapore exposure
incidents.summary: From late December 2025 the Grok chatbot on X was widely used to produce non-consensual sexualised edits of real people. The sources checked do not quantify local complaints in Singapore. The case is included because the service was available and the regulator engaged X.
incidents.notes: Onset date is the start of a documented analysis window of mass misuse; sources vary on the exact start. Local harm not quantified.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Indonesia
incidents.summary: Reports that Grok produced sexualised images of real women and minors led Indonesia's communications ministry to begin investigating in early January 2026.
incidents.source_title: Marketing-Interactive on IMDA and regional action
incidents.notes: Same onset rule as the other Grok cases.

incidents.title: Deepfakes of President Prabowo and Finance Minister Sri Mulyani used in fake aid scams
incidents.summary: Fraudsters used AI-generated videos of senior officials to promise cash aid and collect fees through WhatsApp. One suspect reportedly took about Rp65 million from around 100 victims from December 2024. The OECD incident monitor records a related scam across 20 provinces.
incidents.notes: Onset is 'since December 2024' per the source, so lags are approximate.

incidents.title: Deepfake of Finance Minister Sri Mulyani calling teachers a 'burden'
incidents.summary: A manipulated clip cut from her 7 August 2025 speech falsely showed the minister calling teachers a burden on the state. An official later said false content had fuelled anger and protests; that causal link is the official's claim and is not independently established here.
incidents.notes: Date is the minister's own denial, the earliest public record found.

incidents.title: Deepfake news-anchor and PM videos promote investment schemes on Facebook
incidents.summary: AI-manipulated videos imitating Bernama TV news anchors, and a fake clip of PM Anwar Ibrahim, promoted dubious investment schemes on Facebook after repeated incidents. Earlier circulation is likely, so this is a running series and not a single dated event.
incidents.notes: Onset unknown, so no response lag is computed for this series.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Malaysia
incidents.summary: MCMC recorded 17 complaints or reports about Grok misuse in Malaysia: six formal complaints, two police reports, eight social-media tagging complaints and one First Information Report opened by MCMC. Content involved women and minors.

incidents.title: Deepfake audio of President Marcos 'ordering' military action
incidents.summary: Manipulated audio imitating President Marcos appeared to direct the armed forces to act against a foreign country, during South China Sea tensions and a joint military exercise. Officials said the clip was fake and probably produced by a foreign actor.
incidents.notes: Date is the first official statement, the earliest public record found.

incidents.title: Grok image-tool misuse (sexualised deepfakes): Philippines
incidents.summary: Authorities cited Grok's capacity to generate sexually explicit, non-consensual deepfake material, including content that could involve minors.

incidents.title: Deepfake video-call impersonation scams
incidents.summary: Scammers took over Zalo and Facebook accounts and used the owners' photos and videos to stage fake video calls asking contacts for money.
incidents.notes: Date is the earliest report found.

incidents.title: Deepfake sextortion of individuals and entrepreneurs
incidents.summary: Criminals used face-swapped explicit videos to extort victims, including a Hanoi schoolgirl in March 2024 and entrepreneurs in Ho Chi Minh City in early 2024.

incidents.title: Deepfake Zoom call impersonating PM Wong and other officials costs a victim at least S$4.9 million
incidents.summary: Scammers contacted a business professional on WhatsApp, posing as the Secretary to the Cabinet, and invited him to a fabricated Zoom meeting featuring AI-generated versions of the Prime Minister, the President and other officials. He transferred at least S$4.9 million before realising on 14 May 2026 that it was fake. The date is the Singapore Police Force advisory; the scam began earlier.
incidents.notes: Onset unknown (the money moved in several transfers before 14 May), so no response lag is computed. Also cited in TFGI's Perspectives series on AI readiness (10 Nov 2026).

incidents.title: Thai PM targeted by an AI voice-clone scam impersonating another leader
incidents.summary: Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra said she received a realistic voice message mimicking a well-known ASEAN leader, whom she did not name, asking for a donation and claiming Thailand was the only member yet to contribute. She said she nearly fell for it. The date is her public account; the call came earlier.
incidents.notes: The date of the call itself is not stated in the sources checked, so no response lag is computed.

incidents.title: AI face-altering video-call scam impersonating police, run from a Poipet call centre
incidents.summary: A call-centre gang operating from Poipet, Cambodia, impersonated Thai police on video calls and used AI to alter the callers' faces. Police said it targeted at least 163 people; one victim, a Thai-British beauty queen, lost 4 million baht. Thailand's Central Investigation Bureau arrested two suspects on 2 and 3 February 2025.
incidents.notes: The date is the arrests, the first public record, so the scam itself was earlier and undated. The Star reports the two suspects said they were forced to work for the gang.

incidents.title: AI-generated 'pilot' persona lures a 66-year-old woman to Chiang Mai airport
incidents.summary: A 66-year-old woman from Lampang travelled alone to Chiang Mai International Airport to meet a man she believed was a pilot, then learned he was an AI-generated character on Facebook. The OECD monitor classifies the harm as psychological; the sources listed do not report a financial loss.
incidents.source_title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor, 17 Sep 2026
incidents.notes: Verified from the OECD monitor page and its list of articles; the news articles themselves were not opened. No official response found.

incidents.title: Deepfake videos of JG Summit CEO Lance Gokongwei used to promote fake crypto and forex schemes
incidents.summary: The Securities and Exchange Commission warned that scammers were using deepfake video and audio of Lance Gokongwei, president and CEO of JG Summit Holdings, to endorse fraudulent crypto and forex investments. The date is the SEC warning, the earliest public record found.
incidents.source_title: AI Incident Database 1148 (reports on the SEC warning)
incidents.notes: Verified from the incident-database entry; the SEC advisory itself was not opened. Onset unknown.

incidents.title: AI-assisted romance scams using deepfake personas draw police and CICC alerts
incidents.summary: The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) and the Philippine National Police issued alerts about AI-assisted romance scams, in which scammers use AI-generated personas. The civil-society group Scam Watch Pilipinas cited a retired school principal who lost 2.5 million pesos. This is a running series, not one dated event.
incidents.notes: Verified from search listings and excerpts of the news pieces, not read in full. A repost dated 2 Feb 2026 suggests an earlier CICC warning; not confirmed.

responses.summary: Said on Facebook that he knew of several videos purporting to show him promoting crypto scams, noted that Deputy PM Wong was also targeted, and urged the public not to respond.
responses.notes: One outlet reports the posts as 28 Dec; most say 29 Dec.

responses.summary: Published an advisory on detecting and responding to deepfake scams, built around a '3A' approach: assess the message, analyse audio-visual elements, authenticate content using tools. It cites the December 2023 deepfakes.
Warned the public that a video of him promoting an investment product was a deepfake.
Warned that deepfake videos and voice clones were using his image to sell cryptocurrency, money-making schemes and PR services.

responses.actor: Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI)
responses.actor_role: Ministry, reply to a parliamentary question
responses.summary: Told Parliament that IMDA was engaging X over non-consensual sexualised imagery generated and distributed with Grok.
responses.source_title: MDDI response to Parliamentary Question, 3 Feb 2026
responses.notes: An IMDA spokesperson also told media it was engaging X (X is designated under Singapore's Code of Practice for Online Safety for social media services). That statement is undated in the sources checked, so it is queued for verification and the lag here may be overstated.

responses.actor: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)
responses.summary: Warned that it could ban X and Grok over non-consensual deepfake content.
responses.notes: Source is a news listing page; the article itself was not opened.

responses.actor: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)
responses.summary: Temporarily restricted access to Grok. Indonesia was the first country in the region to do so.

responses.actor: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)
responses.summary: Restored access conditionally after X Corp sent a commitment letter on 31 January listing layered safeguards. The ministry said it could reimpose the ban if violations were found.
responses.source_title: Reuters via New Straits Times, 1 Feb 2026
responses.notes: Outlets date the announcement 1 to 3 February.

responses.actor_role: Police, Director Brig. Gen. Himawan Bayu Aji
responses.summary: Disclosed that police were handling a case of AI deepfake videos using President Prabowo, the Vice President and the Finance Minister, and said police would give Komdigi input for digital-literacy messaging.
Held a press conference on the case: the suspect reportedly made tens of millions of rupiah from the fake social-aid videos.

responses.actor: Police with the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs
responses.summary: Coordinated with the ministry to act on accounts spreading the deepfakes; the Instagram account used for the scam was blocked and taken down.
Said on her official Instagram that she made no such remark and that the video was a deepfake cut from her speech.
responses.notes: One outlet places the clarification on 21 Aug.

responses.summary: Urged social media platforms to tackle a surge of disinformation, citing the Sri Mulyani deepfake and recycled footage of riots.

responses.actor: Ministry of Communications, Deputy Minister Teo
responses.summary: The ministry instructed MCMC to ask Meta to remove AI-manipulated videos of Bernama TV news anchors from Facebook; the deputy minister urged the public to complain to Meta or MCMC.
responses.notes: A takedown request to a platform, not a legal order.

responses.summary: Warned the public against investment scams that use deepfakes to mimic prominent people and reputable companies.

responses.actor: MCMC and the Deputy Communications Minister
responses.summary: Reported that MCMC removed 63,652 pieces of fraudulent content from social media in 2024, about ten times more than the previous year, and cited deepfakes of PM Anwar and the former central bank governor.
responses.notes: Aggregate removals, not deepfake-specific; legal basis not stated.

responses.actor: Royal Malaysia Police (Bukit Aman CCID) and Securities Commission
responses.summary: Police identified five AI-generated deepfake investment-scam videos of public figures including PM Anwar. The Securities Commission said it was working with MCMC to remove them.
Said the ministry was using subsidiary instruments under the Online Safety Act 2025 for enforcement and legal action against social media platforms over deepfake scam advertising.
responses.notes: Linked to this series by theme (deepfake scam ads).

responses.summary: Issued a notice to X Corp and xAI requiring removal of the offending content. MCMC later said no remedial action had been taken.
responses.notes: Date taken from MCMC's statement as reported on 16 Jan; the article itself was not opened.

responses.summary: Issued a second notice to X Corp and xAI.
Imposed a temporary restriction on access to Grok on X as a 'preventive and proportionate' measure.
responses.notes: Sources give 11 or 12 January.

responses.actor: MCMC and the Ministry of Communications
responses.summary: Announced they would take legal action against X Corp and xAI.
Lifted the restriction after considering X's explanations and initial confirmations, subject to continuous monitoring.
Warned that the audio was a deepfake, said no such directive existed, and said it was coordinating with the DICT, National Security Council and National Cybersecurity Inter-Agency Committee.
Ordered the National Bureau of Investigation to investigate the deepfake audio.
Said police had information on the possible source of the deepfake technology used; the DOJ had directed the NBI to hold those responsible accountable.

responses.actor: Department of ICT and Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC)
responses.summary: Announced a ban on Grok and ordered its takedown under the Cybercrime Prevention Act, joining Indonesia and Malaysia.
responses.notes: Sources give 15 or 16 January for the announcement.

responses.summary: Directed internet service providers to block access to Grok nationwide.
Confirmed the restriction was lifted after xAI committed to tighten content controls and remove features that allowed sexually explicit manipulated images.

responses.actor: Department of Cyber Security and High-Tech Crime Prevention, Ministry of Public Security
responses.summary: Described working with the Ministry of Information and Communications and the State Bank on improving personal identification and authentication quality, in response to deepfake scam reports.
responses.notes: The source excerpt was truncated, so the full list of measures is not recorded.

responses.actor: Ministry of Information and Communications (Authority of Information Security)
responses.summary: Official Dispatch 2416/BTTTT/CATTT launched an action-month campaign and a handbook on online-fraud prevention that lists deepfake and deepvoice video-call scams.
responses.notes: Exact issue date not stated in the source.

responses.summary: Dismantled a group using deepfakes to blackmail entrepreneurs and celebrities; the suspects were arrested and equipment seized.
responses.notes: Described as 'early 2024'.

responses.summary: Apprehended the culprits in the March 2024 case of a schoolgirl targeted with a fabricated explicit video.
responses.notes: Date of arrest not stated.

responses.actor: Hanoi Police and Minister of Public Security Luong Tam Quang
responses.summary: Publicly warned of rising AI-driven deepfake extortion. The minister said the ministry was adding technological countermeasures, including a crime-reporting feature on the VNeID app.
Issued a public advisory warning of scams that impersonate senior government officials, including the Secretary to the Cabinet, and disclosed the S$4.9 million case.
Released footage of the fake Zoom meeting and a video explaining the red flags that showed deepfake technology had been used.
Described the attempted scam at a policy meeting and warned the public against AI-powered scams.
Called on ASEAN to tackle online scams and misinformation, a day after describing the attempted scam.
responses.notes: The date follows from 'a day after' in the article listing; the article was not read in full.

responses.actor: Central Investigation Bureau (CIB), Royal Thai Police
responses.summary: Arrested two suspects on 2 and 3 February 2025 under court warrants on charges including defrauding the public by impersonation.
responses.notes: Sources differ by a day on one arrest (2 or 3 February). The later date is used.

responses.summary: Warned the public that scammers were using deepfake video and audio of the JG Summit CEO to endorse fraudulent crypto and forex schemes.
responses.notes: Verified from the incident-database summary; the SEC advisory was not opened.

responses.summary: Warned the public, with the police and Scam Watch Pilipinas, about the rising risk of AI-driven romance scams.
responses.notes: Verified from excerpts. A repost dated 2 Feb 2026 suggests an earlier CICC warning; not confirmed.

responses.summary: Issued a public warning about AI-assisted romance scams.
responses.notes: Verified from the article listing and excerpts.

instruments.title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
instruments.summary: Endorsed at the 4th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting in Singapore. Sets national and regional recommendations with a voluntary, market-driven approach.

instruments.title: ASEAN Working Group on AI Governance (WG-AI)
instruments.summary: Working group formed to drive the guide's recommendations and serve as ASEAN's focal point on AI with outside partners.
instruments.notes: Month taken from a law-firm guide; confirm against an ASEAN source.

instruments.title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics: Generative AI
instruments.summary: Adds nine policy recommendations on generative AI and covers deepfakes, impersonation and fraud among six named risks. Adoption by member states is voluntary.

instruments.title: Hanoi Digital Declaration (6th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting)
instruments.summary: Includes AI commitments: deeper policy harmonisation and joint safety efforts under the WG-AI. It is a general commitment and does not address the Grok case specifically.

instruments.title: Model AI Governance Framework (1st edition)
instruments.summary: Singapore's first voluntary, sector-agnostic framework for responsible AI, released for consultation and adoption.

instruments.title: Model AI Governance Framework (2nd edition)
instruments.summary: Adds robustness and reproducibility considerations and refines the first edition for usability.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy (NAIS 1.0)
instruments.summary: Singapore's first national AI strategy.

instruments.title: AI Verify testing framework and toolkit (international pilot)
instruments.summary: A governance testing framework and open-source toolkit for checking AI systems against 11 internationally recognised principles.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy 2.0 (NAIS 2.0)
instruments.summary: Updates the 2019 strategy, treating AI as a necessity and committing to a trusted environment alongside capability building.

instruments.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
instruments.summary: Sets out nine dimensions for trustworthy generative AI, after public consultation from January to March 2024.

instruments.title: Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act 2024
instruments.summary: Prohibits publishing, boosting, sharing or reposting deepfakes and other digitally manipulated content depicting election candidates, and lets candidates seek review and corrective directions. Introduced 9 Sep 2024, passed 15 Oct 2024.

instruments.title: Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act
instruments.summary: Passed 5 Nov 2025 after introduction on 15 Oct 2025. Creates an Online Safety Commission able to direct takedowns, restrict perpetrator accounts and help victims identify anonymous perpetrators.
instruments.next_milestone: Online Safety Commission operational and Act in effect
instruments.notes: Commencement date not confirmed in the sources checked.

instruments.title: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
instruments.summary: Unveiled by the Minister for Digital Development and Information at the World Economic Forum in Davos. Treats agency as a transfer of decision rights to a system.

instruments.title: Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill 2025
instruments.summary: First read on 14 Oct 2025. Proposes making it an offence to produce or possess intimate images without consent, even where generated with AI.
instruments.notes: Outcome not verified in the sources checked.

instruments.title: National Strategy for AI 2020-2045 (Stranas KA)
instruments.summary: National AI strategy covering ethics and policy; a presidential regulation on AI is meant to build on it.

instruments.title: Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 27/2022)
instruments.summary: Indonesia's general data protection statute, one of the laws used to oversee AI in the absence of an AI-specific law.
instruments.notes: Enactment and in-force dates to verify (see backlog).

instruments.title: Ministry Circular Letter No. 9/2023 on AI Ethics
instruments.summary: Sets ethical principles for AI, including inclusivity, security and transparency. Compliance is not mandatory.

instruments.title: Electronic Information and Transactions (ITE) Law, as amended (2024)
instruments.summary: Core law on electronic information, one of the existing laws to which penalties for AI misuse currently refer.

instruments.title: Draft National AI Roadmap, AI ethics guidelines and Presidential Regulation
instruments.issuer: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs
instruments.summary: Public consultation opened 8 Aug 2025 on the roadmap white paper and ethics guidelines concept; a draft Presidential Regulation followed. In Jan 2026 the minister said it was a priority for presidential signature in 2026.
instruments.notes: The release was pushed back from 2025 to 2026.

instruments.title: National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics
instruments.issuer: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI)
instruments.summary: Non-binding guidance encouraging developers and deployers to adopt responsible AI practices voluntarily.

instruments.title: National AI Office (NAIO) launched
instruments.summary: Agency set up to accelerate adoption and shape AI policy and governance; widely seen as the lead on AI regulation.
instruments.notes: NAIO's own site gives an earlier establishment date (28 August); the launch is dated 12 December 2024.

instruments.title: Licensing of social media and messaging platforms (8 million+ users)
instruments.summary: Platforms with at least eight million users in Malaysia must hold an application service provider class licence. Reports say X fell below that threshold and was exempt.

instruments.title: Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 866)
instruments.summary: Passed by Parliament in December 2024, royal assent 6 May 2025, in force 1 Jan 2026 with age-verification duties and subsidiary regulations. The minister has used its instruments against deepfake scam ads.
instruments.notes: One law-firm note dates the passage to December 2025; the legislative timeline above indicates December 2024.

instruments.title: Proposed AI Governance Bill: public consultation paper
instruments.summary: Consultation paper for what would be Malaysia's first horizontal AI statute, covering AI across sectors. Submissions closed 31 July 2026.
instruments.next_milestone: Bill tabled in Parliament (government has said 2026)

instruments.title: Law on Digital Technology Industry (Law No. 71/2025/QH15)
instruments.summary: The first Vietnamese law to explicitly mention AI, treating it as a strategic technology. Some articles took effect 1 July 2025. Its AI provisions were later replaced by the Law on AI.

instruments.title: Law on Personal Data Protection
instruments.summary: Vietnam's first dedicated personal-data statute, effective 1 Jan 2026 alongside implementing Decree 356/2025/ND-CP.

instruments.title: Law on Artificial Intelligence (Law No. 134/2025/QH15)
instruments.summary: Passed 10 Dec 2025 (429 of 434 votes) and in effect 1 Mar 2026. A risk-based, standalone statute described as the first binding AI law in Southeast Asia. National security and defence uses are carved out.

instruments.title: Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (RA 10175)
instruments.summary: General cybercrime statute. Authorities ordered the 2026 Grok takedown under it. It was not written for AI deepfakes.
instruments.notes: Year of enactment taken from general knowledge; confirm against the statute text.

instruments.title: Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173)
instruments.summary: Foundation of data protection law and one of the cornerstones of the current AI governance regime alongside the national AI strategy.
instruments.notes: Year of enactment taken from general knowledge; confirm against the statute text.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy Roadmap 1.0
instruments.summary: First roadmap, focused on industrial competitiveness.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0
instruments.summary: Updated roadmap adopted after the rapid emergence of generative AI.

instruments.title: National AI Strategy for the Philippines (NAIS-PH)
instruments.summary: Presidential strategy approved by President Marcos Jr., described as the cornerstone of the current regime.

instruments.title: COMELEC Resolution No. 11064: AI and social media in election campaigns
instruments.summary: Regulates AI and social media in digital campaigns for the May 2025 elections: requires disclosure of AI use in campaign material and penalises misuse for disinformation.
instruments.notes: Written for the 2025 elections; applicability to later polls to confirm.

instruments.title: House Bill 10567: Deepfake Accountability and Transparency Act
instruments.summary: Would regulate AI-generated deepfakes with disclosure requirements. Pending in committee; reported as under review as of September 2026.

instruments.title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022-2027)
instruments.issuer: Cabinet of Thailand; Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
instruments.summary: Five-pillar plan covering ethical, legal and regulatory readiness, infrastructure, skills, research and sector adoption. A Prime Minister-chaired national AI committee was set up in August 2022.
instruments.source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, 'Comprehensive Policy: Thailand's AI Governance Framework'

instruments.title: Digital Thailand AI Ethics Guideline (2022)
instruments.issuer: Digital Thailand (Ministry of Digital Economy and Society)
instruments.summary: Non-binding national guideline setting out six ethical principles for regulators, developers, providers and users of AI.
instruments.notes: Sources give 1 March 2022 and 22 March 2022 for different guideline entries, so year precision is used. The issuer is named at ministry level only.

instruments.title: Emergency Decree on Prevention and Suppression of Technological Crimes B.E. 2566 (2023), as amended in April 2025
instruments.summary: The April 2025 amendment, published in the Government Gazette on 12 April, set up a Center for Prevention and Suppression of Technology Crimes that can notify financial institutions of names and wallet addresses linked to technology crime. The final text dropped an earlier proposal to widen the definition to cover forged identity and biometrics.
instruments.notes: The original decree dates from 2023; this entry records the 2025 amendment. Law-firm bulletin; the Gazette text was not opened.

instruments.title: Notification of the Electronic Transactions Commission on Measures to Prevent Technological Crimes for Social Media Service Providers
instruments.summary: Issued under the amended Emergency Decree and in effect from 5 July 2025, it sets duties for social media platforms aimed at online fraud and technology-related crime.
instruments.notes: Law-firm bulletin; the notification text was not opened. Its specific duties are not summarised here.

instruments.title: National Cyber Security Agency AI security guidelines
instruments.summary: Recommendations for protecting AI systems from cyber threats, aligned with ISO/IEC 42001:2023 and the NIST AI risk framework.
instruments.source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, Thailand's AI governance framework
instruments.notes: Month precision from a law-firm summary.

instruments.title: Draft Act on Artificial Intelligence (ETDA public hearing)
instruments.summary: New draft released for a public hearing of about 30 days. It would apply to AI development or deployment affecting people in Thailand, even from abroad; high-risk AI would be designated by royal decree; it adds a regulatory sandbox. An earlier set of draft principles had a hearing in May and June 2025.
instruments.source_title: Tilleke & Gibbins, 'Thailand releases new draft AI Act'
instruments.next_milestone: Outcome of the public hearing and a revised draft
instruments.notes: Law-firm summary; the draft text was not opened. Whether it names deepfakes was not checked.

instruments.title: Memorandum of agreement among the DOJ, PCO and DICT against disinformation and deepfakes
instruments.issuer: Department of Justice; Presidential Communications Office; Department of ICT
instruments.summary: The PCO leads public information, the DOJ legal enforcement, and the DICT technology, cybersecurity and monitoring. The Justice Secretary said the government will distinguish criminal disinformation from protected speech.
instruments.next_milestone: Primary release and any implementing guidelines
instruments.notes: The signing date is not stated in this secondary report, so month precision is used. Look for the DOJ or PCO release.

instruments.title: Declaration on the Establishment of an ASEAN AI Safety Network (ASEAN AI SAFE)
instruments.summary: Leaders agreed to set up a regional network supporting the Digital Senior Officials' Meeting and the Working Group on AI Governance on AI safety. It operates on a voluntary and non-binding basis and acknowledges cross-border AI risks such as misinformation, fraud and content manipulation. Digital ministers adopted it in January 2026, and a Kuala Lumpur secretariat was announced.
instruments.notes: Names fraud and content manipulation generally, not deepfakes, so names_risk is no.

instruments.title: ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA)
instruments.summary: Signed in Manila on 14 November 2026 after negotiations that began in September 2023. Reported to cover digital trade, cross-border data flows, payments, cybersecurity and cooperation on AI, and described as the first legally binding standalone digital economy agreement in the region.
instruments.next_milestone: Entry into force and implementation plan (reports differ: first projects in early 2027, or 180 days after signing)
instruments.notes: Placed in the online-safety layer for its cybersecurity cooperation, though it is a broad digital-economy agreement. The signed text was not reviewed, so whether the AI provisions bind states or only commit them to cooperate is unconfirmed.

events.title: Grok image-generation misuse and regional responses
events.summary: Image-editing features on Grok, built into X, were used from late December 2025 to create non-consensual sexualised edits of real people, including minors. Governments across the region took different actions within about three weeks.
events.caution: The onset date is the start of a documented analysis window of mass misuse; sources differ on the exact start, so day counts are approximate.
events.regional_note: No ASEAN-level action specific to Grok was found in the sources checked. The Hanoi Digital Declaration (16 Jan 2026) holds general AI-safety commitments, not a response to this event.

changelog.change: Version 0.2: added Thailand; 6 new cases (SG-I-05, TH-I-01 to TH-I-03, PH-I-03, PH-I-04), 8 new official responses and 9 new policies (6 Thailand, 1 Philippines, 2 ASEAN including DEFA, signed 14 Nov 2026). Added an aim_url column linking cases to their OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor record. Added coverage and proof-of-concept notices.

Version 0.3: optional cookieless visitor counting with GoatCounter (off by default, nothing is added to the page unless a site code is set). New Visitors tab with a live total, a region view, a country table, referring sites, tab use and downloads, shown only after 30 visits and with groups under 3 merged. New fetch_stats.py and a daily GitHub workflow refresh the country snapshot. No cookies; nothing is counted for Do Not Track, Global Privacy Control or local files.

Version 0.1: first release with 13 cases, 34 official responses and 34 policy instruments across ASEAN, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and the Philippines. Every row has a source link and a confidence rating.
Method decision: any action by a government body or a person with official authority counts as a response (statements, warnings, advisories, investigations, orders, laws).
